what.text: Asian Paints is a leading paint and décor company in India, offering a wide range of products and services. It operates in various segments including decorative paints, home décor, and industrial coatings.

segments.name: Decorative
segments.text: India's leading paint and décor company offering a wide range of products and services, including interior and exterior wall finishes, wood finishes, and waterproofing. This segment contributes ₹30,830.4 Crores, which is 86.8% of revenue.

segments.name: International
segments.text: Catering to a wide cross-section of customers across geographies, this segment contributes ₹3,353.6 Crores, which is 9.4% of revenue.

segments.name: Home Décor
segments.text: Provides a complete one-stop home décor solution, including modular kitchens, bath fittings, and decorative lighting. This segment is part of the decorative and home décor revenue.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.text: Offers high-quality custom-formulated products for the automotive and industrial business. This segment contributes ₹1,332.4 Crores, which is 3.8% of revenue.

trajectory.text: Annual revenue showed a slight decline from FY25 to FY26.
Net profit increased from FY25 to FY26.
Quarterly revenue growth year on year was 16.9% for Sep 2026.

verdict.headline: Asian Paints faces challenges in maintaining margin targets despite revenue growth.

narrative_vs_numbers.text: Management's narrative of maintaining PBDIT margins between 18-20% does not align with the reported numbers, as the Sep 2026 margin was 16%. However, the company did achieve a 16.9% year-on-year revenue growth for the Sep 2026 quarter.

bull.text: Asian Paints achieved a significant year-on-year revenue growth of 16.9% for the Sep 2026 quarter.
The company's free cash flow increased to ₹ 5,604 Cr. in FY26, indicating strong cash generation.
The cash conversion cycle improved to 84 days in FY26, reflecting better operational efficiency.

bear.text: The PBDIT margin for Sep 2026 was 16%, below the management's target of 18-20%.
Borrowings increased significantly to ₹ 4,596 Cr. as of Sep 2026, raising concerns about rising debt levels.
Despite revenue growth, the stock's high P/E ratio of 49.2 suggests it may be overvalued.
